# Reading a star chart

A red flashlight keeps night vision intact while reading charts at the eyepiece. Seeing describes air turbulence, while transparency describes haze and humidity. Collimation aligns the primary and secondary mirrors so stars focus to a sharp point.

## Steps

- The Perseid meteor shower peaks in August and often shows dozens of meteors per hour.
- Collimation aligns the primary and secondary mirrors so stars focus to a sharp point.
- A red flashlight keeps night vision intact while reading charts at the eyepiece.

## Checklist

- A planisphere rotates to show which constellations are above the horizon at a given time.
- Light pollution washes out faint galaxies, so a site with a Bortle class of three or lower is worth the drive.
- A red flashlight keeps night vision intact while reading charts at the eyepiece.
- Seeing describes air turbulence, while transparency describes haze and humidity.

## Open questions

The Perseid meteor shower peaks in August and often shows dozens of meteors per hour. Right ascension is measured in hours along the celestial equator, and declination in degrees north or south of it. Collimation aligns the primary and secondary mirrors so stars focus to a sharp point.

A planisphere rotates to show which constellations are above the horizon at a given time. Seeing describes air turbulence, while transparency describes haze and humidity. A dark adapted eye needs about twenty minutes away from white light to reach full sensitivity. The Orion Nebula is visible to the naked eye as a soft glow in the sword of the hunter.
